# stackorder_outputs (Data Source)

Reads the root-module outputs a stack shares through the Stackorder server, so a stack can use another stack's outputs without access to its state.

Nothing is shared until the producer opts in on its default branch: its `.stackorder.yaml`, or `stackorder.yaml` for every stack of its repository, lists the stacks that may read its outputs under `outputs.readers`. Sensitive outputs are withheld unless the producer also sets `outputs.sensitive: share`, and the data source warns about the outputs withheld.

Values read by a data source are stored in the plan file, which Stackorder uploads as a workflow artifact, and in state. To read sensitive values without storing them, use `ephemeral "stackorder_outputs"` instead, which keeps them out of both and needs Terraform 1.10 or later, or OpenTofu 1.11 or later.

The Stackorder documentation on [shared outputs](https://docs.stackorder.io/configuration/outputs) describes the producer's side, `outputs.readers` and `outputs.sensitive`, in full.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "stackorder_outputs" "vpc" {
  stack = "stacks/prod/vpc"
}

resource "aws_security_group" "cluster" {
  name   = "eks-cluster"
  vpc_id = data.stackorder_outputs.vpc.nonsensitive_values.vpc_id
}

data "stackorder_outputs" "dns" {
  stack = "acme/platform//stacks/prod/dns"
}

output "zone_id" {
  value = data.stackorder_outputs.dns.nonsensitive_values.zone_id
}
```

## Reading values

Each output is an attribute of `values`, and of `nonsensitive_values` unless the producer marks it sensitive, with the type it has in the producer's state: `data.stackorder_outputs.vpc.nonsensitive_values.vpc_id`. A root-module `output` that references `values` must set `sensitive = true`. The data source reads the outputs again in every plan, so a change to a producer's outputs reaches the reader at its next plan.

## Ordering

Stackorder plans and applies a reading stack after the stacks it reads. Its scanner infers that dependency from each `stackorder_outputs` block whose `stack` is a literal string, both in the stack's own directory, the only place it reads `terraform_remote_state`, and in every local module inside the repository that the stack calls, directly or through other local modules; a stack of another repository becomes an external dependency, as with a cross-repository `depends_on`. In a module, a `stack` made only of the module's variables and literal text, such as `var.producer` or `"stacks/${var.env}/vpc"`, counts as literal when the `module` block that calls the module sets each of those variables to a literal string, as `producer = "stacks/prod/vpc"` does; a value that block passes on from its own variables does not count. Any other `stack` built from variables or expressions infers nothing and warns. The scanner fetches no remote module and skips a local source outside the repository, so a block inside a registry, git or other remote module, or inside such a local module, infers nothing and gives no warning of its own. In either case, list the producer under `depends_on` in each reader's `.stackorder.yaml`, which orders the stacks but does not silence the warning about a non-literal `stack`.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `stack` (String) Key of the producer stack. `path` or `path:instance` names a stack of the provider's `repository`, such as `stacks/prod/vpc` or `stacks/prod/apps:blue`; `owner/repo//key` names a stack of another repository of the same Stackorder installation, such as `acme/platform//stacks/prod/dns`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Qualified key of the stack, `owner/repo//key`.
- `nonsensitive_values` (Dynamic) The object of `values` without the outputs marked sensitive. Terraform does not treat it as sensitive, so it can feed arguments that refuse sensitive values, such as `for_each`.
- `values` (Dynamic, Sensitive) Object with one attribute per output the stack serves, named after the output, sensitive outputs included when the producer shares them. Terraform treats the whole object as sensitive. Outputs the producer withholds are absent.
